record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.11. What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian (or pseudo-Riemannian) manifold, and let $H:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ be the geodesic Hamiltonian $H(x,p)=\tfrac12 g^{ij}(x)p_ip_j$ generating the geodesic flow on $T^*M$. A function $F:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ that is polynomial in the fiber variables $p$ is called a polynomial integral of the geodesic flow if $\{H,F\}=0$ with respect to the canonical Poisson bracket on $T^*M$; equivalently, the coefficients of $F$ in $p$ form a Killing tensor on $(M,g)$.

A polynomial integral $F=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}F^{\alpha}(x)p_\alpha$ is said to be quantisable if there exists a differential operator $\widehat F$ on $M$ (acting on, say, half-densities or functions, of order equal to the degree of $F$, with principal symbol $F$) that commutes with the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$ of $(M,g)$, i.e.\ $[\Delta_g,\widehat F]=0$.

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the metric $g$ that ensure every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable in the above sense.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2024–2025) on polynomial integrals of geodesic flows continues to develop existence/classification of Killing tensors and local high-degree polynomial integrals, but no general necessary-and-sufficient condition on a metric guaranteeing quantisability of every polynomial integral has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Local high-degree polynomial integrals of geodesic flows
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs local examples of metrics with polynomial integrals of degrees 3, 4, 5 via semi-Hamiltonian PDE systems; addresses existence not quantisation.
status_evidence.claim: Current research focuses on constructing polynomial integrals; no general quantisability characterization is given.

status_evidence.title: The geodesic flow of a generic metric does not admit nontrivial integrals polynomial in momenta
status_evidence.snippet: Shows genericity of non-integrability for polynomial-in-momenta integrals.
status_evidence.claim: Background result confirming that polynomial integrals are special; quantisation question not addressed.
